summary: Preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style transformations (hex-mangled identifiers such as _0x488df8, per-function string dictionaries mapping keys to literals like 'ldd', '/etc/os-release', 'Alpine', 'bun', 'bun.exe'). At npm install time it fetches the Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, unpacks it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the bundled sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle ('// @bun @bun-cjs') with string-array rotation and hex-mangled identifiers; the declared package source (src/EventManager.ts, ~680 bytes) is a thin @or-sdk/base wrapper that never references math_init.js, so the bundle is not a build artifact of the stated event-manager SDK. The alternate-runtime execution pattern uses Bun to run in-package code that Node-based tooling does not analyze, and the obfuscation of both the loader and the payload hides the runtime behavior. The package's declared purpose (an event-manager wrapper) has no need to pull a second runtime at install and execute a large obfuscated bundle.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
